key_concepts: Constellations are groups of stars that form distinct patterns
Constellations appear to move across the sky each night
Some constellations are visible only during certain months or seasons
Some constellations are visible all year-round
Polaris is the North Star and part of Ursa Minor
Polaris is visible throughout the year and used by navigators to find direction
Big Dipper and Little Dipper are asterisms, not constellations
Ursa Major resembles a big bear and is best seen in spring
Cassiopeia forms a W shape and is visible all year-round in the northern sky
Orion is the Hunter and is visible from November to February
Draco means dragon and is visible in July
